page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-N1 CPU model running at 2.5 GHz. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 64 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

A key feature of the c6gn.8xlarge is its high-speed networking capability, delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 48,563.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,689.0. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show a read-only small block cached speed of 1,894.04 GB/sec, though large block uncached write performance drops to 74.98 GB/sec. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 973.0 and a weak single-threaded gzip compression speed of 20.34 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated physical cores and high network throughput, this instance is designed for network-intensive workloads, multi-threaded applications, and distributed systems. It demonstrates solid performance in database operations, achieving 20,432.0 in PassMark database benchmarks and 38.79 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. The arm64 architecture offers qualitative cost efficiency by delivering balanced multi-core performance and high network bandwidth per resource unit, though workloads requiring strong single-threaded performance or specialized x86 instructions may experience performance trade-offs.
description: The Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized, network-optimized instance powered by 32 dedicated physical cores of the arm64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core) and operates on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU hardware but provides a high baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,563.42 and a PassMark database score of 20,432.0, though single-core performance remains a relative trade-off. This instance is appropriate for network-bound workloads, multi-threaded applications, database operations, and static web serving.
